Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated pilot — recap + SLO clarifications

Hi Alice — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size a pilot that proves your latency and throughput SLOs.

Recap (TL;DR):
- Primary workload: clinical-document summarization + short Q&A over streaming responses for clinician assistant.
- Expected avg request: ~350 tokens in prompt + 150 token completion (avg).
- Peak concurrency observed during pilot window: up to ~40 concurrent sessions in a five-minute burst.

Questions we need to lock down before we size reserved capacity:
1) Latency targets: do you need 95th-percentile <= 250ms for single-turn short Q&A, or is 95p <= 800ms acceptable given the current UX? Please call out different targets for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints.
2) Desired sustained throughput (requests/sec) and acceptable burst headroom (we usually recommend 30–50% buffer).
3) Warm-start / cold-start tolerance: how long can the first-token latency be for a cold cache?
4) Any additional constraints on P99 (heavy-tail) vs P95 we should use for SLO gating?

Attachments: I attached a short SLO questionnaire to make answering the above easier.
[Attachment: edgehealth_slo_questionnaire.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

Proposed next steps:
- You answer the questionnaire (5–10 minutes).
- We run a short synthetic qualification on a sample model variant (A100 FP16 / H100 int8 candidate) for your sample prompts.
- Review results and agree on pilot reserved throughput and duration (2–4 weeks typical).

I copied Lauren and Ben to draft a GPU comparison and an initial pilot scope once you confirm the numbers. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if it's easier.

Best,

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline and a couple of constraints from procurement.

Answers:
- Latency: For the clinician assistant (interactive streaming), target P95 <= 400ms and P99 <= 900ms. For batch summarization jobs (nightly bulk), latency is less strict (P95 <= 5s).
- Sustained throughput: baseline 60 rps across the service (mixed streaming + short completions). Burst headroom: we would like to support 120 rps for short windows (1–5 minutes).
- Cold-start tolerance: first-token up to 1.2s acceptable for cold starts; for warmed instances we want <500ms for first-token.
- P99 gating: procurement insists on metric visibility for P99 and token-level cost reports during pilot.

Procurement note: we need an initial cost estimate for a 30-day pilot showing reserved throughput and the ability to pin a model version. Also please include a short list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2, data isolation options).

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: Dedicated pilot — recap + SLO clarifications

Alex / Lauren — attaching the GPU comparison and initial throughput assumptions. High-level findings (summary):

- H100 (80GB) FP16: best single-token latency for streaming (P95 ~220ms at 40 concurrent streaming sessions with KV cache warm), sustained throughput per GPU: ~140 rps for the Edge Health prompt mix assuming continuous batching and 30ms kernel latency improvements we see on H100 for Llama2-style attention.
- A100 (80GB) FP16: slightly higher latency (P95 ~300ms at same concurrency), sustained throughput per GPU: ~95–110 rps depending on batching window (we assume 20–40ms batching latency tradeoff). More predictable performance for mixed workloads (batch + streaming) vs int8 variants.
- Quantized INT8 candidate (H100-hosted quantized runtime): best cost-per-token scenario, sustained throughput similar to H100 FP16 for short-completion workloads but streaming P95 increases to ~340ms under sustained bursts; better if we allow slightly larger batching windows.
- Smaller GPUs (T4-like 32GB quantized): significantly cheaper but you lose streaming tail latency and concurrency headroom — we'd recommend only for secondary/backup capacity.

Pilot recommendation (narrow):
- Start with 2x H100 (reserved pool), provisioned with autoscale headroom to spin up another H100-sized unit for bursts. Expected sustained capacity: ~260 rps (2 GPUs combined at baseline assumptions), burst capacity to ~400 rps for short windows with fast autoscale.
- If procurement is sensitive to cost, alternate pilot: 3x A100 reserved (baseline ~300 rps combined) — slightly more predictable for batch, but higher per-token cost for streaming.

Assumptions attached in the PDF. Installed KV cache hit-rate assumed at 75% with our LRU prefetching for clinician sessions. Batching window for streaming kept tight (20–30ms) to preserve first-token latency; for batch jobs we open to larger batching.

[Attachment: gpu_options_comparison.pdf (application/pdf)]

Let me know if you want me to add a conservative and an aggressive sizing column — I can drop that in the spreadsheet.

—Ben

- SLO targets for pilot: streaming P95 <= 400ms, streaming P99 visibility (dashboarding) with token-level cost reports daily. Batch summarization P95 <= 5s.
- Observability: daily ingest of latency percentiles, token counts, and cost; weekly checkpoint call to validate quality and rollout plan.
- Compliance: include SOC2 Type II summary, network isolation options (VPC peering), and audit log exports (7-day retention for the pilot per procurement ask).

Estimated cost (30 days):
- Reserved 2x H100: $XX,XXX (reserved capacity premium applied)
- Estimated usage over & above reserved (burst/autoscale) — pay-as-you-go: $X,XXX (estimate)
